text:
morgan: quick daily vuln signal dump — three hits we should act on now, short notes below :eyes:

cve-bot: automated enrichment -> CVE-2025-21876 | httpx | path traversal in URL parsing | CVSS 9.1 / EPSS 0.78 | vendor fixed in 0.24.1 | exploit-db: none public yet | link: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-21876

cve-bot: automated enrichment -> CVE-2025-33110 | uvicorn | request header handling leads to header smuggling / request routing confusion | CVSS 6.5 / EPSS 0.04 | vendor advisory: patch available in 0.18.3 | link: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-33110

cve-bot: automated enrichment -> CVE-2025-41001 | aws-kms-client (internal wrapper) | client-side key-material caching bug could leak encrypted blobs to logs on misconfig | CVSS 8.2 / EPSS 0.12 | vendor: investigation, mitigation recommended: audit & rotate keys | link: internal advisory: https://confluence/redwood/kms-cve-41001

jen: thanks — prioritization proposal: #1 (httpx) critical, emergency patch for any public-facing service that pulls httpx; #3 (kms client) high for secrets posture; #2 (uvicorn) medium/low risk, schedule normal patch cycle unless exploit appears.

kevin: I ran quick exploit searches: no PoC for httpx in exploit-db or GitHub as of now. Shodan scan for our IP ranges returns nothing matching the specific httpx fingerprint. EPSS 0.78 suggests likely opportunistic but not widespread.

tara: owners — assigning: httpx -> @kevin (web-team), uvicorn -> @jen (platform), kms-client -> @dmitri (security infra). Please ack.

kevin: ack. immediate plan for httpx: 1) identify images with vulnerable versions (scan registry), 2) create hotfix branch & patch image with httpx==0.24.1, 3) canary to Dedicated pool, 4) roll over 4h window if metrics clean. I'll post image list in a sec. :thumbsup:

jen: ack for uvicorn. I'll add a middleware rule to enforce strict header parsing as temporary mitigation and schedule release in the weekly patch train if no active exploit.

kevin: registry scan quick output (snip):
```
images-with-httpx:
 - web-service:v2.4.1 -> httpx 0.24.0
 - async-worker:v1.8.0 -> httpx 0.23.5
```
I'll prioritize web-service first (public).

dmitri: kms-client note — impact depends on whether the client was used with logging enabled in prod (we log stack traces for failed decrypts currently). If true, rotate affected CMKs and enable audit streaming for decrypt/Encrypt API calls to our SIEM. Also check HSM/KMS usage logs for anomalous calls since 2025-03-01.

sre-oncall: can help with canary windows. For web-service we can route 5% traffic to a Dedicated canary (low-latency inference pool) and watch latency / 4xx/5xx / error-types for 2h then 25% for 2h. If anything spikes, rollback.

morgan: mitigation checklist for tracking: [ ] patch image + PR link, [ ] canary rollout plan, [ ] enable additional audit logs (kms + http access), [ ] create WAF rule to block suspicious path patterns for httpx vuln, [ ] rotate CMKs if secret exposure confirmed, [ ] update runbook + postmortem placeholder if exploit appears.

tara: tagging SLA windows: httpx -> 48h hotpatch; kms-client -> 72h investigation + mitigation; uvicorn -> normal cadence.

kevin: created PR: https://git/repo/web-service/pull/402 — updates httpx to 0.24.1 and adds a short integration test for URL parsing edge cases. Requesting rapid review from @jen and @sre-oncall.

jen: reviewing now. small comment on test flakiness, will push a fix.

dmitri: starting key-usage query against KMS logs. Will post results in ~30m. If we see decrypts from unexpected principals, escalate to incident channel and rotate.

morgan: also log note — product needs to tighten RBAC on service accounts that can call KMS decrypt; @platform to enforce least-privilege by next week. For now, add temporary deny rule for any non-prod principals calling prod CMKs.

kevin: landed PR and built image: web-service:v2.4.2-canary. Scheduling canary per SRE plan in ~15m.

sre-oncall: starting canary now. watchlist: 5xx errors, increased latencies, & WAF logs. tagging this thread in incidents if anything hits. :eyes:

kevin: canary looks clean after 45m. no anomalies. advancing to 25% slot.

dmitri: KMS query update: 0 hits of suspicious decrypts; all decrypts from expected principals since 2025-03-01. no immediate evidence of leakage. Still recommend audit stream and scheduled CMK rotation in 7 days as a precaution.

morgan: final call — proceed with full rollout for httpx patch (kevin) after 2h at 25% if no regressions. dmitri to enable audit streaming + schedule CMK rotation. jen to merge uvicorn header enforcement as temporary mitigation. Tara to update runbook and set follow-up meeting tomorrow 10:00.

jen: will create small config change for header middleware + release notes.

kevin: will roll to 100% after the last canary window unless someone objects within 30m. :thumbsup:

morgan: thanks team — filing short incident-note placeholder: https://confluence/redwood/sec/incidents/placeholder-httpx-2025-21876

sre-oncall: no regressions observed through full rollout. closing canary monitoring. :white_check_mark:

morgan: closing thread — actions assigned. we'll reconvene if new intelligence appears. :wave:
